hints: At each step, subtract one digit that appears in the current number.
Let dp[x] be the fewest steps to reach zero from x; the chosen digit leads to a smaller state.
Ignore digit 0 because subtracting it makes no progress.
analogy: At each number, choose one of its nonzero digits and ask how many steps remain afterward.
example: For 27, subtract 7 to reach 20, subtract 2 to 18, then 8 to 10, 1 to 9, and 9 to zero: five steps.
algorithm: For x=1..n, set dp[x]=1+min(dp[x-d]) over nonzero decimal digits d of x.
correctness: Every legal first move subtracts one of the available nonzero digits; taking the best resulting state considers every possible first move.
complexity: O(n log n) time for digit extraction and O(n) space.
